Functional Analysis of RNA G-Quadruplex Stabilization and Associated Epitranscriptomic Modification in mRNA Regulation and Dysfunction

Abstract:

Post-transcriptional regulation is a pivotal event in controlling gene expression modulated by various epitranscriptomic modifications and RNA secondary structures, including G-quadruplexes. Recent studies have shown the co-occurrence of various epitranscriptomic modifications with RNA G-quadruplexes (rG4s) and their potential role in regulatory pathways. Herein, we investigated the dynamic changes in colocalization frequency of modification (m5C and &ampPsi ) with potential G-quadruplex forming sequence (PQS) in mouse embryonic stem cell (mESC) and mouse tissues. Furthermore, the RNA binding protein (RBP) analysis is done to identify modification colocalized sites that are targeted by regulatory RBPs supporting their role in gene expression regulation. In addition, the distribution of colocalized m5C and &ampPsi sites with PQS at different functional parts of transcripts have also been investigated. Moreover, analysis of RNA binding protein (RBP) database reveals that many of the colocalized sites are targeted by regulatory RBPs supporting their role in gene expression regulation. Functional validation demonstrated that PDS and COL mediated modulation alters the gene expression, while PDS reduced the viability of cells as a function of concentration. These findings highlight the interplay between epitranscriptomic modification and secondary structure and may facilitate the finding of novel therapeutic targets for genetic illness.
